stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy's Manager of Record is leaving amicably at the end of the month and a successor has been identified. Which statements about the change of Manager of Record application are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The inventory attestation is signed by both the outgoing and the incoming Manager.
The inventory covers Schedules II through V and reportable Schedule VI substances.
A staff pharmacist may sign in place of the outgoing Manager for convenience.
A certified copy of the Drug Store Pharmacy licence accompanies the application.
The Board may require the proposed Manager of Record to appear before it.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 6.10(2) requires an attestation confirming an inventory of all Schedule II through V substances and Schedule VI substances required to be reported to the prescription monitoring program, SIGNED BY THE OUTGOING AND THE PROPOSED INCOMING Manager of Record, together with the ORIGINAL Drug Store Pharmacy licence and the fees. A staff pharmacist may sign only where the outgoing Manager is unavailable through DEATH, SERIOUS ILLNESS OR TERMINATION, on notice of the reason. Under 6.10(1) the Board may require the proposed Manager to appear.

choice_analysis.B: Correct: reportable Schedule VI is inside the inventory.
choice_analysis.C: The substitution is confined to death, serious illness or termination.
choice_analysis.D: The regulation calls for the original licence, not a copy however certified.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: the Board may require an appearance.

related_facts: The Board may find a proposed Manager of Record unsuitable on stated factors
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates treat the departing manager as out of the picture once notice is given.

reasoning_steps: Identify who must sign the attestation
Check what the inventory must cover
Confine the staff-pharmacist substitution to the stated circumstances
